review_notes: Independently reviewed by /root/review_gate/kernel/reviewer-main__melee__ft__ftdrawcommon-1. Read both owned files completely in canonical and rendered form, all subject and outgoing-link pages, all 309 proposal lines, all 138 functionality lines, all 3463 fact-ledger lines, and all 1242 link-ledger lines.

All six proposed writes are supported. The 80080C28 correction preserves the optional x5AC.xC[1] branch; the 80080E18 correction correctly includes eligibility-helper mutation and the additional guards on specialized draws; the three 80081140 corrections distinguish callback assignment from geometry resolution and arbitrary-state restoration; the TU mapping correctly distinguishes local auxiliary dispatch from independently scheduled rendering.

Checked foreign definitions and consumers in ftlib, ftparts, camera, gobj, lbgx, ftdata, ifmagnify, grizumi, lbshadow, ftkirby, ftpurin, and ftafterimage. In particular, ifmagnify.c lines 437–439 independently support the shared-callback assertion in the proposed 80081140 game_mapping, although that proposal's evidence array does not itself include the ifmagnify citation.

The pass conversion is an unchecked lookup into [1,4,2,0], not a bit shift or a validated enum conversion. The active table and callers support passes 0/1/2. Negative and greater-than-three indices have no local protection. Counts cast to unsigned and fighter-kind callback indices likewise require valid caller-owned state.

The damage-offset accessor tests floating values directly: positive and negative zero are false; nonzero values, infinities, and NaNs can activate the matrix path. No finite-value validation occurs. The output matrix is untouched on the false path, and the successful path dereferences the current camera without a null check.

The returned matrix belongs to the caller. The common and specialized routines use stack matrices. The two non-null entries in ftData_UnkMtxFunc0 forward the borrowed matrix into hierarchy display rather than storing it in Fighter state. This is not an ownership transfer or a guarantee concerning arbitrary future callbacks.

The reflection caller resets callbacks even when HSD_CObjSetCurrent fails, provided its image guard was entered. Neither callback setter saves previous callbacks. The shadow helpers similarly select fixed event profiles, not snapshots; event 2 also dispatches group 3, and model-event callbacks are not suppressed merely because a visibility latch already has the requested value.

Acceptance does not prove section membership, compiled layout, lower-resolution assets, historical names, or the authored meaning of the motion-union vector. The independent dispositions below explicitly defer these claims. In particular, the camera-space-origin portion of fact:7add40c3-3f4b-45d7-af6c-62b33dbb75b3 is additionally unresolved rather than proved by its inverse-matrix consumer.
Rendered substitutions are hypotheses only. No source, shared knowledge, public message, or artifact mutation was performed.

unresolved.detail: All fourteen facts on .data, .sdata, and .sdata2 remain unresolved as section claims. Authored types, initializers, and uses do not establish section membership, adjacency, pool size, absolute addresses, or terminal padding. The duplicate .data/.sdata attribution is not resolved by address-like symbol suffixes.

The code casts the address of walk.fast_anim_frame to Vec3* and applies an inverse viewing matrix. Its producer, authored vector identity, and camera-space invariant remain unproved. The source TODO and declarations are not compiled-layout proof. This specifically defers the camera-space-origin portion of fact:7add40c3-3f4b-45d7-af6c-62b33dbb75b3.

Magnify, reflection, and shadow callers demonstrate reuse of event-1 rendering. They do not prove lower polygon counts, lower-resolution model assets, or exclusive meanings for event numbers. No gameplay interpretation is assigned to hurt-state values 1 and 2 beyond the explicit dispatch.

Neither callback setters nor shadow-profile helpers save arbitrary previous state. The exact prior-profile rationale of link:a179f3b2-6b00-4d42-806e-5cf0da40a529 remains unresolved. Retained restore terminology elsewhere refers only to the demonstrated fixed common callback or event-0 profile.

Retained inferred names are semantic hypotheses. Parameter #rN locators are inherited identities, not newly verified physical-register mappings. No compiled ABI or object-layout claim is accepted from header declarations alone.
